blocks.prompt: 11. Let \(g: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}\) be given by \(g(x) = x^{3}\ \ 3x\) [the sign between the terms is missing in print; read as \(x^{3} - 3x\)]. Determine if \(g(x)\) is injective and/or surjective.
blocks.explanation:
Injective doosra naam hai one-to-one ka, aur surjective doosra naam hai onto ka. Dono \(g(x) = x^3 - 3x\) ke liye test karne hain.
Diya kya hai? \(g: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}\), \(g(x) = x^3 - 3x\) (kitab mein beech ka sign chhapne se reh gaya hai; neeche dekhein).
Find kya karna hai? Kya \(g\) injective hai, aur kya surjective hai.
Plan: "injective nahi" dikhane ke liye ek counter-example kaafi hai, values ki chhoti table se; surjective ke liye cubic ke dono kinaron ka rawayya.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(g(x) = x^3 - 3x\), domain aur co-domain \(\mathbb{R}\).
Humein find karna hai: injective? surjective?
Tareeqa: Table bana kar barabar outputs dhoondenge. Phir dikhayenge ke \(x^3 - 3x = y\) har real \(y\) ke liye real hal rakhta hai. Yaad rakhein: kisi property ko "nahi" saabit karne ke liye ek misaal kaafi hai, lekin "haan" saabit karne ke liye har case ki daleel chahiye.

Values ki table
\[g(-2) = -8 + 6 = -2\]
\[g(-1) = -1 + 3 = 2\]
\[g(0) = 0,\quad g(1) = -2,\quad g(2) = 2\]
Kyun: Chhote whole numbers jaldi hisaab ho jate hain aur pattern dikha dete hain. Dhyan se: \((-2)^3 = -8\) aur \(-3 \times (-2) = +6\).

Injective nahi
\[g(1) = g(-2) = -2,\quad 1 \ne -2\]
Kyun: Do alag inputs ka ek hi output aaya, jo one-to-one ki shart tor deta hai. Ek aur misaal: \(x^3 - 3x = x(x^2 - 3)\), is liye \(g(0) = 0\) aur \(g(\sqrt{3}) = 0\) bhi. Graph par horizontal line \(y = -2\) curve ko do jagah kaat'ti hai.

Surjective hai
\[x \to \infty:\; x^3 - 3x \to \infty\]
\[x \to -\infty:\; x^3 - 3x \to -\infty\]
Kyun: Bare \(|x|\) par \(x^3\) wali term \(3x\) se kahin bari hoti hai, is liye wahi faisla karti hai: daen taraf output bohat upar, baen taraf bohat neeche. Graph ek hi silsila (bina toote) curve hai jo \(-\infty\) se \(\infty\) tak jata hai, is liye har horizontal line \(y = c\) ko kam az kam ek dafa zaroor kaat'ta hai. Yani \(x^3 - 3x = c\) (real coefficients wali cubic equation) ka hamesha kam az kam ek real root hota hai.
Dhyan dein: Injective na hona surjective hone ko nahi rokta; dono alag sawal hain.

Tasdeeq: ek misaal
\[c = 18:\; x = 3,\ 27 - 9 = 18 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: Output 18 chuna to input 3 mil gaya. Graph mein bhi dekh lein: line \(y = -2\) do jagah milti hai (injective nahi), aur har horizontal line kam az kam ek jagah (surjective).
blocks.final_answer: \(g(x) = x^3 - 3x\) surjective (onto) hai lekin injective nahi (misaal \(g(1) = g(-2) = -2\)); is liye bijective nahi.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab mein \(g(x) = x^{3}\ \ 3x\) chhapa hai, beech ka sign ghayab hai. Sahi \(g(x) = x^{3} - 3x\) hai: answer key ka jawab "g(x) is surjective" (aur injective nahi) sirf isi par poora utarta hai. Agar plus hota to \(x^{3} + 3x\) hamesha barhta rehta aur injective aur surjective dono hota. (Key ne yeh jawab Sawal 9 wali line par chhapa hai.)
